claim: Splinter's crate layering is declared in architecture.toml with ten tiers from foundation to sample
Only splinter-model is allowed to depend on brain
Only splinter-agent and splinter-model may depend on sven
The command line and every sample depend on the SDK and nothing else of Splinter's
Splinter's AGENTS.md states that neither sven nor brain depends on Splinter
Splinter declares that a model is asked for by role and names the seven roles policy, teacher, generator, planner, judge, critic, router
An experience is immutable: verdicts, rewards, labels and dataset membership are derived facts
A closed-book solve builds a sven engine with no tools
A code-runtime environment gives the solver exactly one tool named run_code
A repository episode uses sven's coding toolset with automatic approval
Every solve runs under Splinter's single SYSTEM_PROMPT
A solve refuses to run in an environment other than the one its task records
An experience is content addressed by the digest of its canonical JSON
Verdicts, step labels and relations are annotations appended beside an experience, never written into it
A reward is derived from verdicts and never stored
Verdict strengths are ordered Judged, Consistency, Formal, Executable, Constraint
Task kinds are graded by one of thirteen verifier kinds
A verifier sees the output and privileged material, never the trajectory
A judge-strength verdict requires a calibrated judge with minimum precision 0.9 and refuses to grade its own model
An executable check passes only when a completion line derived from the digest is seen
The stated-reference verifier allows an answer at most 4 times the reference length plus 60 characters
Mutation validation requires a kill rate of 1.0 over at most 32 mutants
The workspace verifier overlays hidden checks on a fresh copy and fails a patch touching a protected path
The decision rule ignores abstentions, uses only the strongest-rank verdicts and returns no decision when they conflict
Held-out records are taken as whole groups: a tenth of the samples, grown to at least 8 units, at most a quarter
Texts sharing at least 8 distinct runs of 8 words are one group; a run held by more than 6 texts is boilerplate
Task near-duplicates use 3-word shingles with Jaccard overlap at least 0.8
Gate tasks that match a prompt the candidate trained on are excluded and counted as leaked
A training record is refused if it contains a sealed probe's question or shares an 8-word run with a probe
The exposure audit fails an attempt that names a hidden path, a forbidden string, or repeats a 12-token shingle of hidden content
Exam families are reserved before any task is generated; a family needs at least 120 words
Exposed attempts and harness failures are withheld and counted, in no denominator
Datasets are projected from verified experience by twelve views and six objectives
SFT is written as brain generic-messages-v2 and DPO as generic-preference-v1
A dataset manifest names the views, experiences, tasks and sources every record came from and is stored beside the file
The student's turn is the instruction alone: the default strip drops privileged teacher context
Only a task's assistant action is supervised; system and user turns carry train=false
A compacted or pruned trajectory is excluded, not repaired
The training set is capped per concept (0.25), task kind (0.5) and verification strength (0.75)
A monitoring split is taken in whole families, at least 3, default share 0.1
Replay sampling is deterministic by content digest and seed
LoRA SFT is run by brain's ChatFineTune and DPO by brain's PreferenceFineTune
Default LoRA settings: learning rate 2e-4, rank 8, alpha 2 per rank, weight decay 0
The step budget is three passes over the records clamped to 40..2000 steps
Replay of earlier releases takes 0.25 of each earlier release's records and 0.25 of training draws
Rehearsal of the base model's own answers takes 0.25 of draws; half of the rehearsal set is code-graded form tasks
A candidate continues the champion: continue_from is the parent release's adapter
A monitored run keeps the best evaluation's adapter
Consolidation has two modes: full fine-tune of every weight, or merging the adapter into the base
Full consolidation defaults to learning rate 1e-5 and 6 epochs with a retention replay share of 0.25
A generation is consolidated automatically once it holds more than 2000 trained records
Consolidation is carried out by brain's ChatFullFineTune and merge_adapter
The release gate has four checks: improvement, retention, anchor and serve; a candidate passes only if all four pass
A check that was not measured fails with the reason 'not measured'
The improvement check is a one-sided exact paired sign test at alpha 0.05 over discordant clusters, a family counting once
The retention check fails when accuracy on any earlier release's held-out suite drops by more than 0.05
The anchor check fails when accuracy on the frozen anchor suite drops by more than 0.02 and reports a 95% bootstrap interval of 4000 resamples
The serve check requires brain serve to report the candidate's adapter digest and at least 75% agreement on up to 8 re-answered held-out tasks
Repository exams use the same four checks with the exam families as improvement suite and graded-alike verdict agreement for serving
The gate's bootstrap seed is drawn when not given and recorded
A failed retention check re-queues the forgotten concepts for new tasks
Only a candidate trained from the current champion can replace it
A release manifest has format splinter-release-v4 and records artifact, parent, candidate, datasets, replay, rehearsal, training, gate, metrics, terms, provenance and generation
A release is written once; an existing release is refused
Unrestricted distribution is refused unless the terms of everything the candidate was made from permit it
The default alias is policy:default; moving an alias is a compare-and-set from the release the gate measured against
After every alias move the serving manifest <state>/serving/<alias>.json is rewritten so that brain serve --adapter-manifest follows the release
Rollback moves the alias to the release it was trained from and refuses when there is none
splinter lineage walks any artifact up to its source bytes and down to what came from it, derived on every call

A documentation defect found while reading: the command-line README says a release is written under <state>/releases/<hex>/ while the code stores the manifest in the experience database and copies nothing
A source is content addressed (blake3 over its canonical origin and parts) and has one of four origins: document, repository, command, session
A document is one UTF-8 text file of at most 1 MiB; a larger or non-text file is refused
A directory is captured file by file, ignoring .git, target and node_modules, and a file left out is recorded with a reason
A command is run without a shell with a 30 second timeout, a 1 MiB output cap and an environment allowlist of PATH, HOME and LANG
A repository revision is archived as a workspace snapshot of its tracked files, and a dirty tree is refused
A recorded agent session is an ATIF trajectory of at most 64 MiB; unknown ATIF keys and sessions with no user step are refused; secrets are removed and only the fact of removal is recorded
Text is cut into sections that are byte ranges: Markdown at headings outside code fences, other text at blank lines; evidence addresses a section by digest and byte offsets
The generator is shown 3 sections per request
Sources are added from the command line with source add, which accepts a file, a directory or cmd: followed by a command

The built-in model-writable kinds include recall, taught, arithmetic, format, advise, converse, explain, predict, construct, debug, counterexample, transform, classify, retrieve, multi-turn and combine, and workspace-change tasks are made by code and never proposed by a model
The denoise kind is built by code from a source: a window of 12 words with one word dropped and two adjacent swapped, graded by exact match, needing no generator model
A task is admitted only by code; there are twenty-one rejection reasons for model-written tasks

The rejection reasons are malformed, no_reply, over_count, unknown_section, quote_not_found, too_few_sections, unresolved, missing_material, material_not_shown, not_self_contained, wrong_form, ungrounded, not_quoted, checks_failed, test_not_admitted, duplicate, near_duplicate, reference_changed, no_subject, contradiction, invalid
A text answer is grounded when at least 80% of the reference's content words and every number of it appear in the cited evidence
A task must name its subject so that someone who never saw the source gets one answer; a task is self-contained only if it quotes no dropped privileged item of 8 or more words
Two tasks on one subject whose grounded references disagree are both refused
A kind is dropped after 24 proposals if fewer than 0.1 are admitted, and the generator is sent a correction after 3 refusals for one reason, at most 2 corrections
Repository tasks have their own rejection vocabulary including red_baseline, flaky_baseline, equivalent_mutant, tests_not_separable, not_restorable, leaks_change and already_held
The tasks report counts admitted and rejected tasks per kind, rejections by reason, every rejection with detail, and the model calls with their pre-admission candidate counts
A model-written task can be given up to 3 differently worded variants that keep the original's reference, evidence and verifiers; a variant that changes the reference is rejected
Variants are only measured and never trained on; dataset building refuses them
Near-duplicates are found by normalised exact match or 3-word-shingle Jaccard overlap of 0.8 or more, and the same rule filters the training selection
A group smaller than 5% of the pool counts for no cap group, and a selection reports candidates, duplicates, capped and selected
When a retention check fails the forgotten concepts are queued and their sections get new tasks on the next learn
Mastery of a concept is its pass rate over the last 32 decided attempts, and the 5 weakest concepts are listed
Rehearsal is half code-built form tasks and half general requests the base writes, 8 per request; the base answers greedily; requests matching the anchor suite are excluded and repeats refused
A task the policy never solves is solved once more by a teacher shown the source sections it is grounded in
Examination families are reserved by stable hash before task generation, 50 exam and 50 dev families by default, 8 tasks per exam family and 4 per dev family
Per claim, absorb has a model write 12 paraphrases of which 4 are held out for stopping, and 4 statement, 2 reverse and 2 implication forms
A claim of kind procedure is stored and never trained on
A claim is a correction, fact or procedure; claim extraction keeps only claims that every one of 2 passes produced
A claim is admitted by code only when each quote is a verbatim substring of the person's own message at the cited step
Every number, quoted term and name of a claim's statement must occur in the cited words, else it is refused as unsupported_term

The claim refusals are malformed, unknown_step, assistant_evidence, no_user_evidence, quote_not_verbatim, unsupported_term, procedure, wrong_answer_not_said, not_entailed, third_party_personal and duplicate
A ruling is Admitted (with what it supersedes), Reinforced, Forgotten or Refused
Brain's SDK exposes ChatFineTune (LoRA SFT), PreferenceFineTune (DPO) and ChatFullFineTune
The qwen3-family LoRA trainer can hold its frozen base in bf16
The qwen3-family trainer recomputes each layer in the backward pass from its saved residual
The qwen3-family trainer sizes its LM-head logits in chunks (head_chunk_rows) with a chunked weighted cross-entropy
Brain has a causal GQA flash-attention forward and backward supporting head dimension up to 256
Brain's qwen35 crate has a streaming FP8 source that dequantizes in 128-row bands and a BaseDtype enum with F32, Bf16 and Nf4
Brain defines an NF4 weight type with a 16-entry lookup table and a 4-bit NF4 matrix-vector kernel
Brain's make test/gradcheck runs the brain-gradcheck package, which holds finite-difference checks of qwen35 including LoRA
Brain's make test/parity runs the gradient checks on the CPU backend
Brain has finite-difference gradient checks for the flash attention training path at head dimensions 40, 128 and 256
Brain implements the Qwen3.8-27B dense model in its qwen35 crate with Gated DeltaNet and grouped-query attention layers in a 3:1 split
Self-Instruct has a model write its own instructions and filters them before fine-tuning on them
STaR and ReST train on the model's own outputs that a check confirms, repeatedly
LoRA freezes the base model and trains low-rank adapters
QLoRA trains LoRA adapters over a base quantised to 4 bits
DPO optimises preferences without a separate reward model
RAFT trains a model on domain documents with distractor passages
Catastrophic forgetting is the loss of earlier capability when a network is trained on new data
Recomputing activations trades compute for memory in the backward pass
Fused or chunked cross-entropy avoids materialising the logits of a large vocabulary
FlashAttention computes exact attention without materialising the score matrix
Gated DeltaNet is a gated linear-attention layer based on the delta rule
The generator wrote and the funnel admitted 63 tasks from 3 of the 3 text parts of the corpus in 558 seconds
